analysis:
This PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds head lines 874-878. No executable source, config, or deployment change is supplied, so no control is weakened or removed in this diff.

The added text documents two GLM prompt-contract behaviors: (1) reasoning returned by OpenRouter on earlier assistant turns (`reasoning` or `reasoning_details` text) is rendered as the template's `reasoning_content` (`GLM5NextPromptPolicy.RawControls`, `returnedReasoning`); (2) `strict` tools are served by validating each `auto` call against its schema before exposure (`ToolConstraintValidation.validate`), not by constrained decoding. The text states the second behavior is validation only, so it does not overclaim a control. It also keeps the existing statement that the parser does not advertise function calling.

Threat-model relevance: the paragraph describes a request-local prompt rendering path. Prompt content stays within A-001 handling in the provider process (TB-002 and TB-007). The paragraph does not alter the encryption, attestation, prefix-cache, or authorization boundaries (T-041, T-053, T-054). The documented template-hash restriction (`requireShippedTemplate`) is unchanged.

Open integration questions, none a finding: whether the underlying Swift change in `GLM5NextPromptPolicy` is the behavior described. Specifically, whether `returnedReasoning` is injected only from authenticated request fields, whether it respects the cache scope and prompt-contract identity (it changes the rendered token sequence), and whether `ToolConstraintValidation` fails closed on malformed arguments. That code is outside the supplied evidence, so it is not verified here. Other lines in the supplied ranges are unchanged context and were not treated as new.
